IPYNB-SEC-001's 5 obligations all shared one identical, generic, never-individually-verified 3-test citation -- the same never-audited-security-baseline pattern already found and closed for ubl (UBL-SEC-001), nrrd, and xliff (XLIFF-SEC-001) this session. ipynb's actual security posture proved exceptionally strong once investigated: a 4th existing test (test_input_and_decoded_payload_bytes_are_bounded) was already sitting in the cited file uncited, and a separate, rigorous audit-hook-based test file (test_obligation_core_path_no_execution.py, proving the core load/validate/save/diff/upgrade path never executes notebook code even against 5 hostile payloads, with both a runtime CPython audit-hook proof and a static AST-level proof that core modules do not even import the execution adapter) was already complete and simply never cited against these obligations. 4 of 5 obligations promoted to implemented via pure citation correction, zero new tests. Closed this slice with a new _is_safe_resource_filename() guard in adapters/export.py (rejects relative traversal, absolute paths, nested subdirectories, and Windows-style backslash sequences; correctly still accepts a filename that merely starts with dots) plus 7 new tests, then promoted to implemented. implemented_behavior: Unknown fields and vendor metadata namespaces survive round-trips at both notebook and cell level, idempotently across two passes. Unicode content is proven exactly preserved as part of the complete core vector (a lambda character in both metadata and cell source survives serialized == source).
